questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Israel?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Israel article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Israel?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Israel on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “During the modern Common Era” part of the Israel article.

questions.proof: In May 1967, Egypt sent its army near the border with Israel, expelled UN peacekeepers that had been in the Sinai Peninsula since 1957, and blocked Israel's access to the Red Sea.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Israel?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Before the Common Era (BCE)” part of the Israel article.

questions.proof: Around 1400 BCE, another Semitic people called the Hebrews settled in Canaan under the leadership of Moses and Joshua.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “There is a long history of conflict between Israel and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Israel”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Israel article.

questions.proof: There is a long history of conflict between Israel and Palestine.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Isaac Herzog has been the President of Israel since July _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “The President” part of the Israel article.

questions.proof: Isaac Herzog has been the President of Israel since July 2021.
